title: An all-night outing and card game with Pete Johnson
summary: After the show they ate Italian food, watched the five a.m. show, and played cards until afternoon.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I say, "Well, this is luck 'cause cabs kinda hard to get... scarce in the mornin' about two o'clock." So I said, "Well, you made up your mind you gonna go over to the club with me?" Say, "I ain't ready to go to bed. It's too lonesome in my house...in my room...by myself." I said, "I don't sleep good no way till in broad daylight an' then I'll sleep in the daytime but," I say, "I'll go...we'll go over there and see the five o'clock show."

So me and her and Pete Johnson, coupla other o' the band boys got in the car, so we left an' took off. We went in there to where they have I-talian food over there they had...was a I-talian joint they have I-talian food cook. So I just love meatballs and spaghetti. I just loved, to be crazy about meatballs and spaghetti 'cause I was used to eatin' it in Kansas City 'cause I worked with all them I-talians in Kansas City, an' I like the taste of it, so I have me some meatballs and spaghetti, and we had...she had steak or somethin' else. So then we went on back in the back to the nightclub. We set up there and watched the show. So we come out of there just about eight or nine o'clock that mornin'.
Said, "I ain't never been up this late." Said, "Y'all got it." Say, "Now, I'm goin' home, go to bed. I ain't used to bein' out this time o' mornin'...specially in no nightclub."
Say, "Well-l-l-l-l-l, hol' on, don' be in no hurry. Come on
Let's go. Let's go down to the place where you work at." Say, "What time it open?"
Say, "Well, it ain't open right now but they open up about ten o'clock in the mornin'."

I say, "Well, we'll stop by the hotel. You can freshen up, an' we'll go up there...now." I didn't know how to talk to her 'cause she...she didn't drink, so I couldn't say, "Come on, we'll go up there and have a few drinks." So I said, "Well, me and Pete Johnson'll go up there and we'll see if we can catch the boss there this mornin' an' see 'bout gettin' a job when we close over here, the nightclub where we're workin' at, Ethel Waters's place.
So she say, "Well, he generally be up there early in the mornin', checkin' up, so...wait'll I change my clothes an' I'll take you...I'll go with you-all up there."

So we left and went to the hotel. She got...changed her clothes, freshened up, and then she went with us to the nightclub. We sit around up there and had lunch. Was about eleven o'clock in the mornin' so we went to the restaurant, had lunch. I say, "Well, it's time for me to go home now and git inta bed."
"Yeah, it time for me to go home and get into bed, too... 'cause I got to get up at about nine o'clock and go back to work, an' I miss my rest."
Well, I live 'cross the hall from her. Pete Johnson live upstairs. Me 'n' Pete Johnson went on home. Pete Johnson had his wife with 'im. So, we went home and sit in the lobby for awhile, an' we

talked and rapped, haha'd...heehee'd, back an' forth, so she said, "I'm gonna see y'all fellows. Y'all...y'all got it." 'Cause she went in her room and went to sleep. So I went upstairs with Pete Johnson, an' a bunch o' cats come by there, an' we started playing cards, playin' Dirty Hearts, so we fool aroun' up there till about two o'clock in the afternoon, playin' cards an' we drinkin', havin' a good time, an' no worry about no goin' to sleep. That never crossed my mind.
